Let $\omega$ be an indeterminate, set $A=\omega^{-2}$, and put $k'=\mathbb Q(\omega)$, $q_K=A^2$, and $q_L=A^{-2}$. Work over the scalar extension to $k'$ of the library Hopf algebra at $q_L$. The parameter and Cartan-generator conversion from Korinman's convention is $q_L=q_K^{-1}$ and $K_L=K_K^{-1}$; the root generators $E,F$ correspond unchanged. The vector basis order remains $(v_+,v_-)$. Korinman displays $\rho(E)=\begin{pmatrix}0&0\\1&0\end{pmatrix}$ and $\rho(F)=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\0&0\end{pmatrix}$; converting those displayed action matrices to the column-action convention used here transposes them. Thus the module matrices are
$$E=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\0&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad F=\begin{pmatrix}0&0\\1&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad K_K=\begin{pmatrix}q_K&0\\0&q_K^{-1}\end{pmatrix}.$$
Equivalently, for the library parameter use $K_L=K_K^{-1}=\operatorname{diag}(q_L,q_L^{-1})$ and the library coproduct convention $\Delta(E)=E\otimes K_L^{-1}+1\otimes E$, $\Delta(F)=F\otimes1+K_L\otimes F$. The parameters $q_K$ and $q_L$ are not identified.

The object $V$ is absolutely simple in the $k'$-linear representation category.

Korinman's §2.2 matrix
$$C_K=\begin{pmatrix}0&\omega\\-\omega^5&0\end{pmatrix}$$
is an equivariant map $V^*\to V$ in its indicated dual and vector bases. It is a duality isomorphism, not an endomorphism of $V$, so it is not the matrix of $\Omega^{-1}$.

To specify the half-ribbon action, use the Snyder–Tingley convention $q_{\mathrm{ST}}=q_K$, $K_{\mathrm{ST}}=K_K=K_L^{-1}$, $E_{\mathrm{ST}}=E$, and $F_{\mathrm{ST}}=F$ in the same ordered basis. Since $q_K=\omega^{-4}$, choose $q_{\mathrm{ST}}^{1/4}=\omega^{-1}$. Let $X=JT_{w_0}$ be their half-ribbon element and let $\Omega$ be its operator on $V$. On the fundamental highest- and lowest-weight vectors, their formula gives $Xv_+=-q_{\mathrm{ST}}^{3/4}v_-$ and $Xv_-=q_{\mathrm{ST}}^{3/4}v_+$. The half-ribbon action therefore gives the actual inverse matrix and its square:
$$\operatorname{Mat}_{(v_+,v_-)}(\Omega^{-1})=\begin{pmatrix}0&-\omega^3\\\omega^3&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad \Omega^2=-\omega^{-6}\operatorname{id}_V=-A^3\operatorname{id}_V.$$
Snyder–Tingley’s associated Hopf-algebra ribbon element is $X^{-2}$; the positive categorical twist in this Kauffman-bracket convention is its inverse $X^2=\Omega^2$. In the ordered basis $(v_+\otimes v_+,v_+\otimes v_-,v_-\otimes v_+,v_-\otimes v_-)$, the positive braiding is
$$c_{V,V}=\begin{pmatrix}A&0&0&0\\0&0&A^{-1}&0\\0&A^{-1}&A-A^{-3}&0\\0&0&0&A\end{pmatrix}.$$
Its ribbon quantum dimension is $\delta=-A^2-A^{-2}$. The half-ribbon and universal $R$-matrix are those of the topological half-ribbon representation category; the selected ribbon element is the Kauffman-bracket one, not the usual $U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ ribbon element.

Let $v_+^*,v_-^*$ be the ordinary dual basis. The left-dual action on $V^*$ is the contragredient action $(x\cdot f)(v)=f(S(x)v)$ for the antipode $S$ of the stated library Hopf convention. Identify the displayed copy of $V$ with this left dual $V^\vee$ by $v_+\mapsto v_-^*$ and $v_-\mapsto -A^{-2}v_+^*$. In this identification the evaluation and coevaluation maps are
$$B(v_+\otimes v_-)=1,\quad B(v_-\otimes v_+)=-A^{-2},\quad B(v_+\otimes v_+)=B(v_-\otimes v_-)=0,$$
$$U(1)=-A^2v_+\otimes v_-+v_-\otimes v_+.$$
These are the explicit duality maps used in the closure trace.

The positive Artin generator is drawn with braid height increasing upward; the left input strand ends on the right, and the right input strand passes over it:

```tikz
\begin{tikzpicture}[baseline=(current bounding box.center),scale=.8]
  \draw[->] (0,-1) -- (.46,-.08);
  \draw[->] (.54,.08) -- (1,1);
  \draw[->] (1,-1) .. controls (.72,-.5) and (.28,.5) .. (0,1);
  \node at (-.2,-1) {$i$};
  \node at (1.2,-1) {$i+1$};
\end{tikzpicture}
```

The uninterrupted strand in the drawing is the overpassing strand. This is the crossing convention for the displayed matrix; the proof below uses its matrix entries and the half-ribbon source formulas, not the drawing.

Let $A$ be an indeterminate, put $q=A^4$, $q_K=A^2$, and $q_L=A^{-2}=q_K^{-1}$, and work over $F=\mathbb Q(A)$. An oriented knot in $S^3$ means a smooth embedded circle with an orientation, considered up to orientation-preserving ambient isotopy. For an integer $r$, put
$$[r]=\frac{q_K^r-q_K^{-r}}{q_K-q_K^{-1}},\qquad [m]!=\prod_{r=1}^{m}[r]\quad(m\ge1),\qquad [0]!=1.$$
For each $N\ge1$, put $q_N=\exp(2\pi i/N)$.
For each integer $N\ge1$, let $V_N$ have basis $v_0,\ldots,v_{N-1}$ and define the $U_{q_L}(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ action in the library coproduct convention by
$$K_Lv_j=q_L^{N-1-2j}v_j,\qquad Ev_j=[N-j]v_{j-1},\qquad Fv_j=[j+1]v_{j+1},$$
where $v_{-1}=v_N=0$. In the universal $R$-matrix formula use $q_K$ and $H v_j=(N-1-2j)v_j$; on $V_N\otimes V_N$ its action is the finite sum
$$\mathcal R_N=q_K^{H\otimes H/2}\sum_{r=0}^{N-1}q_K^{r(r-1)/2}\frac{(q_K-q_K^{-1})^r}{[r]!}\,E^r\otimes F^r,$$
and the positive crossing is $c_N=P\mathcal R_N$, where $P(x\otimes y)=y\otimes x$. This is an irreducible module of dimension $N$. Equip these matrices with the Kauffman-bracket half-ribbon data: the twist matrix is the scalar $\theta_N=\lambda_N I$ with $\lambda_N=(-1)^{N-1}A^{N^2-1}$, and the matrix $G_N=(-1)^{N-1}\operatorname{diag}(A^{2(N-1-2j)})_{j=0}^{N-1}$ is the pivotal comparison used in the closure trace. The resulting generic quantum dimension is
$$d_N=\operatorname{Tr}(G_N)=(-1)^{N-1}\frac{A^{2N}-A^{-2N}}{A^2-A^{-2}}.$$
Use the contragredient left-dual action $(x\cdot f)(v)=f(S(x)v)$ on $V_N^*$, with evaluation $\operatorname{ev}(f\otimes v)=f(v)$ and coevaluation $1\mapsto\sum_{j=0}^{N-1}v_j\otimes v_j^*$. The ambient category is the $F$-linear category generated by the modules $V_N$ for all $N\ge1$ under finite tensor products, contragredient duals, finite direct sums and images of module-idempotents, whose morphisms are module homomorphisms, and whose tensor-product action is induced by the stated Hopf coproduct; its tensor unit is $F$ with the trivial action, so its tensor-unit endomorphism ring is $F$. These matrix data satisfy the ribbon-category axioms: braiding and inverse braiding, both duality snakes, monoidal pivotal comparison, balancing and dual compatibility of twist. Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice for the framed-tangle and Markov constructions. An oriented knot $K\subset S^3$ presented as the closure of an $n$-strand braid $\beta$ has generic normalized value
$$J_N^{\mathrm{gen}}(K;q)=\lambda_N^{-w(\beta)}\frac{\operatorname{Tr}(G_N^{\otimes n}\rho_N(\beta))}{d_N}\in F,$$
where, for a word $\beta=\sigma_{i_1}^{\varepsilon_1}\cdots\sigma_{i_m}^{\varepsilon_m}$ with $\varepsilon_j\in\{1,-1\}$, $w(\beta):=\sum_{j=1}^m\varepsilon_j$, and $\rho_N(\beta)$ is obtained by replacing each positive braid generator by $c_N$ on the corresponding adjacent tensor factors and each inverse generator by $c_N^{-1}$, then composing in word order. This quotient is an integral Laurent polynomial in $A^4$. Define the **normalized colored Jones sequence** by the unique $J_N(K;q)\in\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$ satisfying $J_N(K;A^4)=J_N^{\mathrm{gen}}(K;A^4)$. Its root value $J_N(K;q_N)$ is obtained by substituting into this Laurent polynomial. The variable transport to the ordinary Jones convention is $t=q^{-1}=A^{-4}$.

1.4 The displayed sum for $d_N$ is a geometric sum, so $d_N=(-1)^{N-1}[N]$. Its numerator $A^{2N}-A^{-2N}$ is a nonzero Laurent polynomial and its denominator $A^2-A^{-2}$ is nonzero in $F$; hence the generic normalization is defined. The Hopf coproduct [F2] supplies the tensor-power action used in $\rho_N(\beta)$. By the braiding, dual, and ribbon axioms [F3] and the all-color ribbon identities [F7], the comparison on $V_N^{\otimes n}$ is $G_N^{\otimes n}$. The basis coevaluation and evaluation in the left categorical trace [F5] then give the ordinary matrix trace $\operatorname{Tr}(G_N^{\otimes n}\rho_N(\beta))$, which is the scalar of the framed closure. 1.2 The strand permutation of $\sigma_1^3$ is $(12)^3=(12)$, so its two endpoints are interchanged; pairing each bottom endpoint with the top endpoint in the same position therefore produces one component.
